output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So, I have some news (it's good news, Dad, keep reading)

Ok. I've been sitting on this for a month and I can't do it anymore, so here goes.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business with my name on it.

Some backstory first. Marisol told me on October 6th that she was closing Rosebud Lane at the end of October, and it's closed now. I'm not going to get into her reasons, that's her business, but she was really clear it had nothing to do with the work and nothing to do with me. I shot for her for four years. Pretty much everything I know about this job I learned standing next to her at a wedding, watching her get a grumpy groomsman to laugh in about four seconds, or seeing her notice the light was about to go perfect ten minutes before anyone else did. Marisol, if you ever end up reading this, thank you. I wouldn't be doing any of this without you.

Then she did something I'm still kind of stunned by. She started telling her 2027 couples that I'm the one they should book. Who does that?? She told me I'd been ready for two years. I don't know about that, but I can tell you I've been planning this in my head for about that long. Notes app lists, spreadsheets at 1am, the whole thing. So when it actually happened it was scary, but it wasn't out of nowhere.

Here's where things stand:

I filed the LLC on October 22nd. Fernhollow Photo LLC. I did it on my lunch break, sitting in my car in a Fred Meyer parking lot, and yes I cried a little. In my defense it was a big moment and the Fred Meyer was very beautiful.

The website went live November 1st.

I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six of those are couples Marisol sent my way, and the other eight found me on their own, which still feels unreal to type. They've all signed contracts and the deposits are coming in. June is going to be wild with four weddings, and the farthest one is out at Wallowa Lake in September, so I guess I'm finally going to see Wallowa Lake.

The best part: my first booking that was 100% mine, with no referral, is Dahlia and Ken. They're getting married at Timberline on June 12th. They found me through the couple photos I took at Multnomah Falls, which are some of my favorite pictures I've ever made. When the email came in that said "We're in!!" I read it like six times. Sam can confirm.

Jae is going to second shoot the big weddings with me. Some of you met Jae at Bree's shower. Jae is amazing and absolutely won't let me miss the grandma crying during the vows.

And now the part I need certain people to read twice.

DAD. I HAVE HEALTH INSURANCE. 🙂

I picked a marketplace plan on November 5th and it starts January 1st, so there's no gap. I know you've been worried about this for basically my whole career, and I love you for it, and it's handled. I thought about the school portrait thing too, I promise I did. But this is what I'm good at and what I want to do, and I'd rather try it now while I'm 32 and my knees still mostly work.

Is it scary? Yeah. Of course it is. This is the first time it's all on me. But I'm not jumping off a cliff with my eyes closed. I have a plan, I have bookings, I have Jae, I have Sam, and I have a lot of people in my corner. Mostly I'm really excited, and I want you guys to be excited with me.

Ok, the name. Some of you have probably guessed this already.

Grandma, this one's for you. Fernhollow is for the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures, with your Pentax, when I was a kid who wouldn't stop asking to borrow it. You let me use up a whole roll of film on moss and a slug and probably your thumb. I don't think I've ever told you this, but that's where all of this started. When I was trying to come up with a name nothing else even came close. So every time somebody says "Fernhollow," they're kind of saying thank you to you. I love you so much.

Also, the celebration cake. Sam surprised me with a cake that said FERNHOLOW, one L, in big blue letters. He swears it was the bakery. The bakery swears it was the order form. We ate the whole thing anyway, and it was delicious, and I took about forty pictures of it. It's the official first Fernhollow typo and I'm putting it in the company history.

Now an offer, which is really more of a request.

I'm bringing the camera to Ruthie's on the 26th, and if anyone wants family pictures, they're free. Your family, your kids, a picture of you and your spouse that isn't a blurry selfie, you and the dog, whatever. Uncle Greg, you can bring a fish if you want, I won't judge (that canyon sunset shot from Maupin was really good by the way, I have notes but they're nice notes). We'll do it before dinner while the light is still decent and everyone still looks put together, so maybe 2 or 2:30. Comment below so I can make a little list and nobody gets skipped.

Bree, I know Juniper is still tiny and you're still in survival mode, so no pressure at all. But whenever you're ready, newborn pictures are on me, forever, no discussion. I'll wash my hands a LOT.

And Mom, yes, Sam is coming, and yes, we're bringing the rolls and the cranberry thing. Leaving by 1:45, Sam's driving, he's already made me promise I won't leave the camera bag in the trunk.

That's the big news. I wanted you to hear it from me first, here, instead of in pieces over the mashed potatoes. If you have questions, ask! I'm happy to talk about it. I'd just rather talk about it excited than worried.

Thank you for always cheering me on, even when I was the kid making everyone stand in the cold for the group photo. (I'm still going to make everyone stand in the cold for the group photo. Some things don't change.)

Love you all. See you at Ruthie's.

Tessa
Fernhollow Photo (two L's)
